mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.5% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates sustained accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate below 4.0% signals an overheating labor market that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the following 5 trading days as investors price in rate hikes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE is below 4.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above 12-month moving averages indicates robust economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as earnings growth expectations rise.
failure_condition: The joint PAYEMS and HOUST signal fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, strong GDP growth (GDPC1) and rising housing starts (HOUST) signal sustained consumer spending, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as earnings momentum is priced in.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 and HOUST are above 12-month moving averages during late-cycle periods.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output, which typically correlates with stronger corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days as the market discounts improved economic activity.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth fails to generate positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: 12-month CPIAUCSL change below 2.5% indicates stable inflation that supports continued low interest rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as monetary accommodation is sustained.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL 12mo % change is below 2.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales (RSAFS) reflect robust consumer spending that boosts corporate revenue growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as earnings outlooks improve.
failure_condition: RSAFS growth fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In tight labor markets (UNRATE < 4.0%), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over 5 trading days due to heightened expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes to cool economic overheating.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE is below 4.0% over a 3-year rolling window.
